items.title: General Electric vs. Joby Aviation: Which Industrials Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: GE Aerospace and Joby Aviation represent two contrasting investment approaches in aviation: GE is an established, profitable aerospace leader generating $7.3B in free cash flow with a 19% net margin, while Joby is a speculative early-stage electric air-taxi company burning $564M annually while awaiting FAA certification. The article recommends GE for proven returns and stability, while suggesting Joby only as a small speculative position in a diversified portfolio.

items.title: BigBear.ai vs. QuantumScape: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares two speculative early-stage tech stocks: BigBear.ai, which provides AI decision intelligence software to government and defense sectors, and QuantumScape, which develops solid-state batteries for electric vehicles. While both are unprofitable, BigBear.ai is recommended as the better choice due to its existing government revenue stream and improving margins, whereas QuantumScape remains in pre-commercial development with significant manufacturing challenges ahead.

items.title: Huntington Rewards Shareholders With Higher 2027 Buyback Plan
items.summary: Huntington Bancshares (HBAN) plans $550 million in share repurchases for 2026 and $1.3-$1.4 billion for 2027, increasing buybacks by $200 million due to a recalibrated lower loan-growth outlook of 6% versus previous 8%-9% expectations. The company maintains strong liquidity of $16 billion and has $2.95 billion remaining under its $3 billion repurchase authorization. Acquisition synergies from Veritex and Cadence integrations are generating stronger-than-expected revenue synergies, supporting earnings growth and shareholder returns.

items.title: Berkshire After Buffett: Can It Continue to Endure and Compound?
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway completes its leadership transition with Greg Abel becoming CEO on January 1, 2026, while Warren Buffett steps into a chairman emeritus role and his son Howard G. Buffett becomes chairman. Despite concerns about the transition, the company's strong financial position with $370B+ in cash and Treasury holdings, decentralized operating model, and high-quality business portfolio across insurance, railroads, utilities, and manufacturing provide continuity and support long-term value creation.

items.title: GE Vernova vs. Oklo: Which Industrials Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares GE Vernova, an established power generation company generating 25% of global electricity with $38.1B in revenue and zero debt, against Oklo, a pre-revenue advanced nuclear reactor developer backed by Meta and Switch. While Oklo shows promise with high-profile agreements and differentiated technology, GE Vernova is recommended as the better 2026 buy due to its proven profitability, strong cash flow, record backlog, and immediate market relevance, whereas Oklo remains years away from commercial revenue and regulatory approval.

items.title: Can M&T Bank's Loan Growth & AI Push Drive Earnings Momentum?
items.summary: M&T Bank raised its 2026 average loan guidance to $141-$143 billion driven by healthy commercial demand. The bank is strengthening fee-based businesses in capital markets, wealth management, and mortgage placement to diversify revenues. AI deployment in underwriting, fraud detection, and cybersecurity is expected to drive productivity gains. Earnings are projected to grow 13.1% in 2026 and 9.5% in 2027.

items.title: Here's Why You Should Hold Corpay's Stock in Your Portfolio Now
items.summary: Corpay (CPAY) has surged 35.6% over six months, driven by strong Corporate Payments organic growth of 16% in Q2 and 43% spend increase to $95 billion. The company projects 2026 revenue growth of 17.4% and EPS growth of 28.2%, supported by cross-border expansion and robust cash generation. However, challenges include slowing U.S. Vehicle Payments growth at 8% and limited margin expansion due to continued investment in sales and product development.

items.title: INTU's Big Bets Keep Scaling: Can These Become Its Main Growth Engine?
items.summary: Intuit's 'Big Bets' (Assisted Tax, Money, and Mid-Market) represent 30% of fiscal 2026 revenues with over 30% year-over-year growth, significantly outpacing overall company growth of 14%. While the company sees a $300B+ addressable market and leverages AI across 82 million consumers and 10 million businesses, new customer acquisition fell short of expectations in fiscal 2026. Management guides fiscal 2027 revenue growth of 9%-10% while continuing to invest in scaling these growth engines.

items.title: Nucor Projects Higher Q3 Earnings on Improved Steel Pricing
items.summary: Nucor Corporation (NUE) announced Q3 2026 earnings guidance of $5.55-$5.65 per diluted share, up from $5.04 in Q2, driven by higher selling prices in its Steel Mills segment and increased volumes and pricing in Steel Products. The company continues share buybacks, having repurchased 2.03 million shares in Q3 at an average price of $247.04. Raw Materials segment performance is expected to weaken due to lower pricing and shipments.

items.title: Can Carnival's Fuel Efficiency Create a Lasting Margin Tailwind?
items.summary: Carnival Corporation (CCL) achieved over 5% fuel efficiency improvement in Q2 fiscal 2026, enabling net income to rise 20% to $569M despite a 30% fuel price increase. The company expects structural cost savings and technology efficiencies to support margin expansion, though fuel volatility remains a constraint. Competitors Royal Caribbean and Norwegian Cruise Line are also pursuing cost management strategies through operational efficiencies and fuel hedging.

items.title: ASML reports transactions under its current share buyback program
items.summary: ASML Holding N.V. conducted share repurchases totaling approximately €428 million across five trading days (September 14-18, 2026) under its current buyback program announced on January 28, 2026. The weighted average repurchase price ranged from €1,389.45 to €1,432.07 per share.

items.title: Here’s Why Amazon's $220 Billion in Capital Spending Shouldn’t Worry Investors.
items.summary: Amazon increased its 2024 capital expenditure forecast to $220 billion to support AI infrastructure growth. CEO Andy Jassy argues this spending is justified, comparing it to early cloud computing investments. With AWS generating $25+ billion in AI revenue run rate and $169 billion total annual run rate, plus multi-year AI contracts providing earnings visibility, the company expects strong financial returns within 3-6 years as data centers monetize.

items.summary: The article argues that while Palantir is a prominent defense tech company, investors should consider RTX and Northrop Grumman instead. RTX and Northrop offer more direct exposure to the defense spending boom through mission-critical hardware and long-term contracts with massive backlogs ($289B and $104.7B respectively), compared to Palantir's software-focused approach which carries a lofty valuation with limited margin for error.

items.title: Looking for Steady Passive Income? This S&P 500 Dividend Stock Pays You Monthly.
items.summary: Healthpeak Properties (DOC), a healthcare REIT, offers a 6% dividend yield with monthly payouts of $0.10 per share. The stock has gained 27.5% in 2026 following strong Q1 results that beat earnings and revenue forecasts. Management raised full-year FFO guidance twice, signaling confidence. However, REITs face headwinds from rising interest rates and bond competition. The company benefits from long-term demographic trends favoring healthcare and senior housing demand.

items.title: Applied Materials vs. Nvidia: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Applied Materials and Nvidia as semiconductor investment options. Nvidia dominates with $215.9B revenue and 55.6% net margins but faces valuation concerns and AI boom dependency. Applied Materials offers more stability with $28.4B revenue and lower valuation multiples but slower growth. The author recommends Applied Materials as the safer choice, citing concerns that AI growth may slow and regulatory threats could impact Nvidia.

items.title: Hims & Hers Health, Inc. Class Action Lawsuit Seeks Recovery for Investors; November 2, 2026, Deadline - Contact Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP
items.summary: A securities fraud class action lawsuit has been filed against Hims & Hers Health, Inc. for material misstatements regarding deceptive privacy practices. The FTC accused HIMS of sharing customers' medical information with third-party advertisers including Meta and Snap. Following the FTC lawsuit announcement on July 29, 2026, HIMS stock declined 14.73%. Investors who purchased HIMS securities between August 4, 2025 and July 29, 2026 can seek lead plaintiff status by November 2, 2026.

items.title: PNR 13-DAY DEADLINE ALERT: Pentair plc Investors with Substantial Losses Have Opportunity to Lead Shareholder Class Action Lawsuit Before October 2, 2026 Lead Plaintiff Deadline
items.summary: Hagens Berman has expanded a securities fraud class action lawsuit against Pentair plc, alleging the company made materially false statements about its financial health and channel inventory from March 11, 2025 to July 14, 2026. On July 14, 2026, Pentair shocked investors with a massive revenue miss ($930M vs. $1.14B forecast), revealed $170M in Pool segment inventory destocking, slashed full-year guidance, and announced the sudden departure of its CFO after only four months. The stock plummeted 15% the following day. Investors with substantial losses have until October 2, 2026 to become lead plaintiffs.

items.title: AppLovin (NASDAQ: APP) Faces Securities Class Action Amid Concerns Over Model Improvements -- HBSS
items.summary: AppLovin Corporation is facing a securities class action lawsuit for allegedly misleading investors about AI model improvements and revenue uplift during Q2 2026. After management promised substantial model improvements and acceleration on the May 6 earnings call, the company revealed in August that uplift was lighter than expected, causing the stock to plunge 19.6% and erasing $44 billion in market capitalization. Investors who purchased shares between February 12 and August 5, 2026 are eligible to join the class action with a November 16, 2026 deadline.

items.title: Warren Buffett Is No Longer Berkshire's Chairman. Here’s Why I'm Buying the Stock Anyway.
items.summary: Warren Buffett has stepped down as executive chairman of Berkshire Hathaway, with his son Howard assuming the chairman role. However, the author argues this is not a thesis-changing event, as the market already priced in Buffett's departure when he stepped down as CEO in May 2025. CEO Greg Abel is effectively deploying capital through buybacks and acquisitions, and Buffett built a durable culture and leadership structure designed to outlast him.

items.title: Anthropic IPO: 1 Key Lesson Investors Can Learn From SpaceX
items.summary: SpaceX's IPO experienced significant volatility after investors grew concerned about the company's massive AI spending ($28.5B capex with 86% going to AI infrastructure) despite modest revenue ($12.5B). Historical data shows large IPOs average only 3.5% returns over 12 months despite strong first-week gains. The article warns that Anthropic's upcoming IPO could face similar investor skepticism regarding heavy AI infrastructure spending, suggesting investors should wait rather than buy at IPO launch.

items.title: Warren Buffett Watched Alphabet's Stock Price Climb 9,000% Before He Decided to Invest. Here's Why He and Greg Abel Are Making It One of Berkshire Hathaway's Biggest Investments Now.
items.summary: Warren Buffett admitted to missing out on a 9,000% gain by not investing in Alphabet earlier, citing his historical avoidance of IPOs and tech stocks. However, he and CEO Greg Abel have now made Alphabet one of Berkshire Hathaway's largest investments, beginning in Q3 2025. Buffett is impressed by Alphabet's massive $200 billion capital expenditure on AI data centers, which Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian says have payback periods under two years, translating to roughly 20% annualized returns. With the stock trading at less than 17 times forward earnings, further purchases are expected.

items.title: ALIBABA DEADLINE: ROSEN, THE FIRST FILING FIRM, Encourages Alibaba Group Holding Limited Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action First Filed by the Firm – BABA
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed a securities class action lawsuit against Alibaba Group Holding Limited, alleging the company made false and misleading statements regarding its control by the Chinese Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT), its classification as a Chinese military company under the NDAA, and undisclosed risks of AI model distillation attacks. Investors who purchased Alibaba securities between June 26, 2025 and June 24, 2026 may be eligible for compensation. The lead plaintiff deadline is October 5, 2026.

items.title: Is Arm Holdings Still a Hidden Winner of the AI Chip Race?
items.summary: Arm Holdings, which licenses CPU designs rather than manufacturing chips, is positioned as a crucial but underappreciated player in the AI infrastructure boom. The company collects royalties on every unit shipped and is expanding beyond smartphones into data centers, where major tech companies like Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Nvidia build Arm-based CPUs. With recent revenue growth of 23-24% and higher royalty rates from newer architectures, Arm has outperformed Nvidia over the past three years, though its valuation at 55x sales remains richly priced.

items.title: ROSEN, TOP RANKED GLOBAL COUNSEL, Encourages AST SpaceMobile, Inc. Investors with Losses in Excess of $100K to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - ASTS
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed class action lawsuits against AST SpaceMobile, Inc. and other companies on behalf of investors who suffered losses. The lawsuit alleges that AST SpaceMobile made false statements regarding its capital requirements, competitive position, and user adoption rates, leading to investor damages when the true details emerged.

items.title: PENTAIR DEADLINE: ROSEN, NATIONAL INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Pentair plc Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - PNR
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is reminding investors who purchased Pentair plc (NYSE: PNR) shares between March 11, 2025 and July 14, 2026 of the October 2, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline in an ongoing securities class action. The lawsuit alleges that Pentair made materially false statements regarding its 80/20 program, which allegedly failed to improve operations, damaged customer relationships, caused loss of market share particularly in the Pool segment, and created undisclosed financial risks.

items.title: Sam Altman Admits the AI Industry Has Done "a Terrible Job" Explaining Its Benefits Amid Growing Backlash. Should That Worry Nvidia and Microsoft Investors?
items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman acknowledges the AI industry has failed to effectively communicate its benefits to the public, contributing to growing backlash against AI stocks. However, the author argues this is a temporary communication problem, not a fundamental flaw, and predicts the market will eventually embrace AI as it did with smartphones and social media. The real question remains which AI platform will emerge as the dominant winner.

items.title: These 15 Words From Amazon’s Andy Jassy May Eliminate Nvidia’s Biggest Risk
items.summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy stated that customers will continue using Nvidia chips for the foreseeable future and that AWS will remain the best place to run Nvidia products. This statement addresses investor concerns about competition from Amazon's custom chips and suggests the AI chip market is large enough for multiple players to succeed without displacing Nvidia's market leadership.

Baidu's stock fell significantly after reporting disappointing financial results in February and August 2026, with the AI-powered business showing deceleration in growth. The lead plaintiff deadline is November 13, 2026.

items.title: Jensen Huang Maintained His Prediction That AI Infrastructure Spending Will Hit $3 Trillion to $4 Trillion by 2030 -- the Same Forecast He Made a Year Ago to the Day. Is Nvidia Still a Buy at These Levels?
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reiterated his forecast that global AI infrastructure spending will reach $3-4 trillion by 2030. Despite Nvidia's massive growth (106% YoY revenue increase, 70% guidance for next year), much of this expected growth is already priced into the stock. Trading at a P/E of 27, the article argues Nvidia remains a buy given its market dominance, expanding addressable market, and diversification beyond GPUs into complete computing systems and strategic investments.

The lawsuit alleges that senior executives engaged in undisclosed activities requiring Board review, raising doubts about disclosure controls and the company's ability to timely file earnings reports. Investors who purchased securities between April 15, 2026 and August 17, 2026 may be eligible for compensation.

items.title: 2 Stocks to Buy as Google Starts Selling Its AI Chips
items.summary: Alphabet has begun selling its custom AI chips (TPUs) to customers for the first time in Q2, creating a new revenue stream. Broadcom supplies the chips and benefits from TPU sales across all deployment scenarios. Both companies are positioned to capitalize on growing AI infrastructure demand, with Broadcom showing accelerating AI semiconductor revenue growth (221% YoY) and Alphabet's Cloud segment posting strong profitability improvements.

items.title: ROSEN, SKILLED INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages AppLovin Corporation Investors with Losses in Excess of $100K to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action – APP
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed a class action lawsuit against AppLovin Corporation on behalf of investors who purchased securities between February 12, 2026 and August 5, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that AppLovin made false and misleading statements regarding its generative AI video creative feature, overstated AI model improvements, and misrepresented the benefits of its 'virtuous cycle' value proposition. Investors with losses exceeding $100,000 are encouraged to contact the firm before the November 16, 2026 deadline to serve as lead plaintiff.

items.title: This Questionable Berkshire Hathaway Holding Actually Makes Sense
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway's investment in Macy's may appear questionable given the retail apocalypse, but the department store chain is showing signs of stabilization. With five consecutive quarters of comparable sales growth (2.7% last quarter), improving guidance, and a low P/E ratio of 8, the investment makes sense as a turnaround play rather than just a real estate bet. The worst of the department store industry's decline appears to be over.

items.title: ExxonMobil's Advantaged Assets and Refining Strength Drive Outlook
items.summary: ExxonMobil (XOM) is well-positioned to capitalize on elevated crude oil prices near $100/barrel and tight refining markets. The company expects advantaged assets (Permian, Guyana, LNG) to represent 65% of upstream production by 2030. XOM plans to maximize refinery throughput to benefit from elevated refining margins. Other energy players like Par Pacific Holdings and ConocoPhillips are also positioned to benefit from favorable market conditions.

items.title: Apple TV's Emmy Sweep Adds Momentum to AAPL's Services Business
items.summary: Apple TV won 29 Emmys at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards, with Apple Originals accumulating 917 total wins and 3,827 nominations. Apple's Services revenue grew 12% to a record $30.74 billion in the June quarter with a 75.6% gross margin. The company surpassed 1.5 billion paid subscriptions supported by over 2.5 billion active devices. However, Apple faces intense competition from Netflix and Disney in the streaming space.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges EquipmentShare.com Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against EquipmentShare.com Inc. (NASDAQ: EQPT) alleging that the company and its officers made materially false statements and failed to disclose undisclosed related-party transactions with entities owned by co-founders. The complaint claims the company's financial statements were misleading regarding these transactions. Investors who purchased securities during the IPO on January 23, 2026, or between January 23-June 23, 2026, are eligible to join the case.

items.title: BMY vs. ARGX: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
items.summary: Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY) is positioned as a superior value opportunity compared to Argenex SE (ARGX) in the biomedical and genetics sector. BMY has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with a forward P/E of 9.10 and Value grade of A, while ARGX has a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) with a forward P/E of 34.19 and Value grade of C. BMY's lower valuation metrics and stronger earnings outlook make it the more attractive value play.

items.title: Nordson (NDSN) Down 6.9% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Rebound?
items.summary: Nordson reported strong Q3 fiscal 2026 earnings with adjusted EPS of $3.25 (beating estimates by 5.2%) and revenues of $817.67 million (up 10.3%), driven by broad organic growth across all three segments and record sales. Despite the solid results, the stock has declined 6.9% since the earnings report. The company raised full-year guidance and maintains a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating with upward estimate revisions, suggesting potential for recovery.

items.title: Lowe's (LOW) Down 10.7% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Rebound?
items.summary: Lowe's reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $4.40, beating estimates of $4.22, but revenues of $25.96B missed the $26.14B consensus. The company lowered its fiscal 2026 outlook citing weak DIY demand and current macro trends. Shares have declined 10.7% since earnings, and the stock received a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating with downward estimate revisions of -7.5%.

items.title: Can GFS' Marvell Deal for SiGe Capacity Expansion Accelerate Growth?
items.summary: GlobalFoundries has signed a multi-year agreement with Marvell Technology to expand silicon germanium (SiGe) production capacity at its Burlington, Vermont facility. The expansion will support next-generation optical transceivers and networking solutions for AI and cloud data centers. GFS shares have outperformed the industry over the past year, though the company faces competition from UMC and TSMC in the optical connectivity market.

items.title: 3 AI Stocks Stuck in Neutral to Buy Before Their Next Catalysts Hit
items.summary: Broadcom, Meta Platforms, and Microsoft are all trading near breakeven for 2026 despite strong fundamentals. Broadcom's custom AI chip business is positioned for rapid growth with major commitments from Alphabet and Anthropic. Meta's new Muse AI agent offers new revenue opportunities through processing and affiliate fees. Microsoft's Azure cloud business continues robust growth with a $679 billion backlog and strong Copilot adoption.

items.title: Buffett Steps Down as Berkshire Enters a New Era
items.summary: Warren Buffett has stepped down as Chairman Emeritus of Berkshire Hathaway after 64 years of ownership and 61 years of leadership. His 71-year-old son Howard assumes the chairman role while CEO Greg Abel continues managing business operations. The conglomerate holds diverse investments across railroads, insurance, and consumer goods.

items.title: 31% of Berkshire Hathaway's Portfolio Is Concentrated in These 2 AI Stocks Under Greg Abel
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway has concentrated 30.7% of its $365 billion equities portfolio in two AI stocks: Apple and Alphabet. Under new CEO Greg Abel, the conglomerate is signaling a bullish stance on AI, with Apple leveraging its 2.5 billion active devices for consumer AI adoption and Alphabet leading across AI research, chip design, and cloud services.

items.title: Here's Why You Should Hold on to Republic Services Stock for Now
items.summary: Republic Services (RSG) reported strong pricing power with 6.4% core price growth driving 90 basis points of Q2 margin expansion, outpacing cost inflation. The company raised 2026 adjusted free cash flow guidance to $2.54-$2.575B and increased its quarterly dividend. However, the company faces ongoing volume pressure with organic volumes declining 1.9% year-over-year and residential volumes expected to remain negative through 2027. Environmental Solutions segment showed promise with sequential revenue gains and margin expansion.

items.title: LULU Falls 14.1% in a Month: Can New Growth Levers Help Investors?
items.summary: lululemon athletica (LULU) shares fell 14.1% over the past month as the company grapples with weakening demand, margin pressures, and lowered fiscal 2026 guidance. Revenue declined 4% YoY to $2.4 billion with comparable sales down 9%, particularly in the Americas. The company is pivoting its product strategy toward newer away-from-body bottoms while core leggings sales dropped 20%. Despite improved valuation metrics, the stock carries a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) due to weaker earnings trends and limited visibility on sales recovery.

items.title: Can Rising Adoption of Agentic AI Accelerate NET's Revenue Growth?
items.summary: Cloudflare is experiencing strong growth driven by AI agent adoption, with over 50% of network traffic from nonhuman sources in Q2 2026. The company's Workers platform added nearly 2 million developers and launched new monetization tools for AI transactions. However, the stock trades at a significantly elevated valuation multiple compared to peers, with a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.summary: Schall, Brown & Schwartz LLP announced a class action lawsuit against GoDaddy Inc. for alleged violations of securities laws. The firm claims GoDaddy made false and misleading statements about its customer strategy, emphasizing short-term contracts despite claiming to focus on growth, which resulted in sharply decelerated bookings growth. Shareholders who purchased shares between September 3, 2025 and February 24, 2026 are encouraged to participate, with a deadline of October 20, 2026.

items.title: IBM Software Growth Slows: Will Recurring Revenue Support Recovery?
items.summary: IBM's Software segment revenues grew 5% to $7.8 billion in Q2 2026, but organic growth was flat due to customers shifting spending toward infrastructure. However, Hybrid Cloud revenues grew 11% with OpenShift ARR reaching $2.2 billion, and the Data business surged 19%. Despite revenue headwinds, IBM expanded Software segment profit by 9% to $2.5 billion with margin expansion of 110 basis points.

items.title: Snowflake's Product Revenue Accelerates: Can It Outpace DELL & ORCL?
items.summary: Snowflake reported strong fiscal Q2 product revenue growth of 37% to $1.49 billion, with AI products driving roughly half of the acceleration. The company raised fiscal 2027 product revenue guidance to $6.07 billion (36% YoY growth) and added 692 net new customers, bringing total customers to 14,554. Snowflake faces competition from Dell Technologies and Oracle, both expanding their AI capabilities, but maintains a strong position in enterprise data and AI markets.

items.title: SEC Opens U.S. Door to Tokenized Stocks: Is Robinhood a Buy Now?
items.summary: The SEC's September 17 Innovation Exemption creates a five-year pathway for tokenized U.S. stocks to trade on blockchain-based venues, potentially benefiting Robinhood Markets. However, Robinhood must adapt its existing Stock Token infrastructure to meet SEC requirements for shareholder rights and voting privileges. While this presents a long-term growth opportunity, competitors like Coinbase and Intercontinental Exchange are advancing similar platforms, intensifying competition. The development is viewed as an incremental strategic positive rather than an immediate earnings catalyst.

items.title: This Dividend King Yielding 4X the S&P 500 Looks Like a Buy Right Now
items.summary: PepsiCo, despite underperforming the S&P 500 over the past five years, is presented as an attractive buy for income investors due to its Dividend King status (55 years of consecutive dividend increases), 4.3% yield (4x the S&P 500), defensive business model resilient to rate hikes, and strategic positioning in growing energy drink market through its 11% stake in Celsius Holdings.

items.title: Bull of the Day: AXT (AXTI)
items.summary: AXT, a semiconductor substrate manufacturer, is positioned as a critical supplier for AI data-center optical interconnects, particularly in indium phosphide (InP) substrates. The company reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $47.6M (up 165% YoY) with 44.9% gross margins and a 170% EPS beat. With a >$100M backlog, planned capacity expansions to $35M quarterly by end-2026 and $65-70M by 2027/early 2028, and progression toward 6-inch wafers, AXT is transitioning from a cyclical substrate maker into a critical AI infrastructure supplier. However, risks include potential slowdown in AI optical spending, China export controls, and margin sustainability.

items.title: Is Verizon the Year's Best Telecom Stock?
items.summary: Verizon Communications has undergone a significant turnaround in 2026 under new CEO Dan Schulman, beating quarterly expectations and achieving 184,000 postpaid net phone additions. The company's acquisition of Frontier Communications boosted fiber broadband connections by 43% year-over-year, while targeting $5 billion in cost cuts. Verizon's stock has risen over 25% this year with expanding EBITDA and margins, positioning it as a potential top-performing telecom stock compared to competitors T-Mobile and AT&T.

items.title: Why Intel Stock Jumped 7.6% Today
items.summary: Intel stock surged 7.6% after Reuters reported that SK Hynix is exploring a potential deal to lease or form a joint venture at Intel's Ohio manufacturing facility. While talks remain exploratory with no formal agreement, the news boosted Intel for two consecutive trading sessions. The potential partnership could provide a significant customer for Intel's struggling Foundry business, though regulatory hurdles remain a concern.

items.title: Oracle vs. Broadcom: Which "Picks and Shovels" AI Stock Has the Bigger Growth Runway From Here?
items.summary: Oracle and Broadcom are critical AI infrastructure players that have underperformed over the past year but show strong growth prospects. Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue is projected to grow from $58B (fiscal 2026) to $230B (fiscal 2028), while Oracle's cloud infrastructure revenue jumped 121% with $664B in remaining performance obligations. Broadcom offers faster earnings growth, while Oracle provides a cheaper entry point into the AI boom.

items.title: Qualcomm Faces Margin Pressure From Rising Costs: Can it Recover?
items.summary: Qualcomm is experiencing significant margin compression in its QCT business due to higher semiconductor input costs, weaker smartphone demand, and unfavorable product mix. The company expects QCT EBT margins to decline to 23-25% in Q4 fiscal 2026 from 26% in Q3, with fixed-price contracts delaying benefits from price increases. Apple-related revenue is expected to decline 50% sequentially, while competitors Intel and AMD are showing stronger performance in data center and AI segments.

items.title: GOOGL Down 7% in the Past 3 Months: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: Alphabet (GOOGL) shares have dropped 7% in three months due to massive AI infrastructure investments doubling capex to $44.9B and resulting in negative free cash flow of $5.855B. While the company faces competition in cloud and search, and regulatory headwinds, Google Cloud revenue surged 82% to $24.8B with a $514B backlog. The stock is rated a Hold with balanced risk-reward, as investors await proof that AI investments translate into sustainable free cash flow growth.

items.title: Can Centene Sustain Its Turnaround Amid Membership Pressure?
items.summary: Centene Corporation reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.51, marking a significant recovery from a loss a year prior, driven by improved medical cost trends and better execution. The company expects Medicaid membership to decline 8%-9% in 2026, but profitability improvements in Marketplace and Medicare segments, combined with higher Medicaid rates and cost initiatives, support continued recovery. CNC reaffirmed its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance above $4.80.

items.title: Can Worldpay Help Global Payments Build a Stronger Growth Story?
items.summary: Global Payments (GPN) has completed its Worldpay acquisition, becoming a pure-play commerce solutions provider. Q2 2026 results showed 33.8% revenue growth to $3.2 billion with normalized revenue growth of 4% and a 70 basis point margin improvement to 42%. The company projects 2026 normalized revenue growth of 4-5% and adjusted EPS of $13.60-$13.80, with successful integration and newer commerce offerings expected to drive future acceleration.

items.title: Lennar Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates on Housing Weakness, Revenues Lag
items.summary: Lennar Corporation reported disappointing Q3 fiscal 2026 results with adjusted EPS falling 38.5% to $1.23 and revenues declining 8.6% to $8.05B. Home deliveries fell 3.4% and average selling prices declined 2.9%, with incentives reaching 12%. The company cut its full-year fiscal 2026 delivery target to 80,000-81,000 homes from 82,000-83,000 due to continued interest-rate pressure and weaker market conditions.

items.title: Insider Sale: CEO Dumps More Than 16,000 Shares of Financial Stock
items.summary: John Q. Doyle, CEO of Marsh & McLennan Companies (MRSH), sold 16,656 shares worth approximately $3.1 million on September 2, 2026, through a pre-arranged Rule 10b5-1 trading plan. The sale represents exercised options originally granted in 2017. Following the transaction, Doyle retains approximately 117,000 shares valued at $21.94 million. The article notes that while MRSH has shown strong revenue and cash flow growth, the stock has underperformed the S&P 500 with a 3.8% CAGR versus 12.5% for the broader market, and rising net debt presents concerns.

items.title: BTSG Faces $200M IRA Hit but Efficiency May Protect Profitability
items.summary: BrightSpring Health Services' Home and Community Pharmacy segment experienced an 8% revenue decline to $540M in Q2, with the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) accounting for approximately $50M of the impact. Despite a projected $200M revenue headwind in 2026 from IRA pricing changes, the company expects only a $15M EBITDA impact, demonstrating that operational efficiency gains from technology, automation, AI, and Lean initiatives are offsetting regulatory pressures. Peer companies Cardinal Health and CVS Health are similarly navigating IRA-driven revenue pressures while maintaining profitability through service agreements and operational improvements.

items.title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT Bernstein Liebhard LLP Announces A Securities Fraud Class Action Lawsuit Has Been Filed Against AST SpaceMobile, Inc. (ASTS)
items.summary: Bernstein Liebhard LLP has announced securities fraud class action lawsuits against three companies: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) for investors who purchased shares between March 4, 2025 and July 15, 2026; Baidu (BIDU) for shareholders between November 18, 2025 and August 17, 2026; and Lincoln Educational Services (LINC) for shareholders between May 11, 2026 and August 9, 2026. The lawsuits allege materially false and misleading statements regarding business operations, growth prospects, and financial stability, resulting in artificially inflated stock prices and investor losses.

items.title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT Bernstein Liebhard LLP Announces A Securities Fraud Class Action Lawsuit Has Been Filed Against Baidu, Inc. (BIDU)
items.summary: Bernstein Liebhard LLP has filed securities fraud class action lawsuits against Baidu, Inc., AST SpaceMobile, Inc., and Lincoln Educational Services Corporation. items.title: CoreWeave Boosts Agentic AI With Multi-Rack NVIDIA Vera Rubin Clusters
items.summary: CoreWeave is expanding its AI infrastructure capabilities by deploying multi-rack NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 clusters and introducing new storage features including cross-region write acceleration and a lower-cost Archive tier. These developments aim to support large-scale agentic AI workloads, though CoreWeave faces intensifying competition from Microsoft and Nebius Group in the AI cloud infrastructure market.

items.title: Greg Abel Has 75% of Berkshire Hathaway's Portfolio Invested in Just 8 Stocks. Is the 1 That's Lagging Behind the S&P 500 the Best Buy Now?
items.summary: Under new CEO Greg Abel, Berkshire Hathaway has concentrated 75% of its $365.2 billion equity portfolio into 8 stocks. American Express is the only one lagging the S&P 500 over the past year due to margin compression from high cardholder rewards and marketing expenses. Despite these headwinds, the article argues American Express offers compelling value at 19.7x trailing earnings for long-term investors who believe in its business model.

items.title: Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller Dumped Broadcom and 11X'd His Fund's Stake in This Trillion-Dollar Dual-Industry Leader
items.summary: Billionaire investor Stanley Druckenmiller exited his entire position in Broadcom during Q2 2026, likely taking profits after a 50%+ gain in just months. Simultaneously, he massively increased his Amazon stake by 1,083%, betting on the company's high-margin AWS cloud business which is experiencing 37% sales growth driven by AI adoption. Druckenmiller's moves suggest caution on near-term AI hype while favoring Amazon's valuation and long-term growth potential.

With strong Q3 results showing 7% revenue growth, $5 billion in new contracts, and raised 2026 guidance, the company is well-positioned to capitalize on growing power demand from AI data centers. However, near-term margin pressure from integration costs presents a near-term risk.

items.title: ROSEN, A LEADING LAW FIRM, Encourages Baidu, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - BIDU

Investors who purchased during the class periods may be eligible for compensation.

items.title: Ultrasound AI Market Size to Surge to USD 22.03 Billion by 2035 at a CAGR of 26.62% – SNS Insider
items.summary: The global Ultrasound AI market is projected to grow from USD 2.09 billion in 2025 to USD 22.03 billion by 2035, with a CAGR of 26.62%. Growth is driven by deep learning advancements, point-of-care imaging adoption, and sonographer shortages. North America leads with 45.54% market share, while Asia-Pacific shows the fastest growth at 28.57% CAGR. Hardware dominates at 48% market share, with software as the fastest-growing segment.

items.title: Kirby McInerney LLP Alerts Investors Who Acquired GoDaddy Inc. GDDY Securities Between September 3, 2025 and February 24, 2026 of Pending Lawsuit
items.summary: Law firm Kirby McInerney LLP is alerting investors about pending securities class action lawsuits against GoDaddy Inc., Taboola.com Ltd., and Alarum Technologies Ltd. The GoDaddy lawsuit alleges the company failed to disclose that a $4.99 promotional pricing strategy for one-year domain contracts would materially impact bookings growth, which fell to 5% in Q4 2025, causing the stock to drop 14% on February 24, 2026. Lead plaintiff deadlines range from October 5-20, 2026.

items.title: Kirby McInerney LLP Alerts Investors Who Acquired Alibaba Group Holding Limited BABA Securities Between June 26, 2025 and June 24, 2026 of Pending Lawsuit
items.summary: Law firm Kirby McInerney LLP announced pending securities class action lawsuits against Alibaba Group Holding Limited, Taboola.com Ltd., and Alarum Technologies Ltd. The Alibaba lawsuit alleges the company made false statements regarding its control by China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and engaged in unauthorized AI model distillation attacks. Stock prices declined significantly following disclosure of these issues in June 2026. Investors have until specified deadlines in October 2026 to seek lead plaintiff status.

items.title: Pentair plc (PNR) Investors: Securities Fraud Class Action Filed, Contact Hagens Berman Before October 2, 2026 Lead Plaintiff Deadline
items.summary: A securities fraud class action lawsuit against Pentair plc has been expanded to cover March 11, 2025 – July 14, 2026. The lawsuit alleges the company made false statements about its financial health and omitted critical information regarding channel inventory destocking in its Pool segment. On July 14, 2026, Pentair shocked investors with a massive revenue miss ($930M vs. $1.14B forecast), slashed full-year guidance, and announced an abrupt CFO departure. The stock plummeted 15% the following day.

items.title: Salesforce vs. Figma: Evaluating the Better High-Growth Software Stock to Buy in 2026
items.summary: The article compares Salesforce and Figma as investment options in 2026. Salesforce, the dominant CRM leader, offers proven profitability with $41.5B revenue, 18% net margins, and $14.4B free cash flow, trading at a reasonable 23.3x P/E ratio. Figma, a rapidly growing design platform, shows 41% revenue growth but remains unprofitable with a negative 118.4% net margin and trades at a premium 66.2x forward P/E. The author recommends Salesforce as the better investment due to its financial stability, competitive moat through AI capabilities, and reasonable valuation, despite acknowledging Figma's impressive growth trajectory.

items.title: Detroit CIOs and CISOs to Examine AI Governance, Cybersecurity Resilience, Enterprise Transformation and the Rise of the "CEO of Technology" at HMG Strategy’s September 24 Summit
items.summary: HMG Strategy is hosting its 17th Annual Detroit C-Level Technology Leadership Summit on September 24 at Orchard Lake Country Club, bringing together CIOs, CISOs and senior technology executives from leading organizations across Detroit, Southeast Michigan and Ontario, Canada. The summit will focus on critical topics including AI governance, Agentic AI, cybersecurity resilience, enterprise transformation and the evolving role of the "CEO of Technology." Attendance is complimentary for qualified senior technology executives.

items.title: Hock Tan Just Guided Broadcom's AI Revenue to Reach $230 Billion by 2028. Should You Believe Him?
items.summary: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan projects the company will generate $230 billion in annual AI semiconductor revenue by fiscal 2028, representing more than a tripling from current levels. The article argues this forecast is credible given Tan's track record of underestimating growth and Broadcom's secured supply chain. The analysis suggests potential 150% upside if the company achieves these targets with a 50% profit margin.

items.title: PLUG's Margins Show Signs of Recovery: Can It Sustain the Momentum?
items.summary: Plug Power reduced its Q2 net loss to $190.1 million from $228.7 million year-over-year and significantly improved gross margin to -0.9% from -30.7%, driven by pricing gains, cost reductions, and operational efficiency. However, the company remains unprofitable with a net loss of $436.1 million for the first half of 2026. The company continues restructuring efforts to improve profitability and liquidity.

items.title: Can CAH Navigate IRA Pricing Changes Risk Without Margin Pressure?
items.summary: Cardinal Health expects fiscal 2027 IRA pricing changes to create similar revenue headwinds as 2026, but management aims to preserve compensation and maintain profitability through distribution agreements and operational efficiency. Peers BrightSpring and CVS Health also face IRA-related revenue pressure but are offsetting impacts through operational improvements and specialty pharmacy growth.

items.title: Visa vs. Mastercard: Which Payment Stock Has More Upside?
items.summary: Visa and Mastercard both benefit from the secular shift toward digital payments and cross-border transactions. While Visa shows strong value-added services growth (34% YoY) and expanding AI-driven services, Mastercard demonstrates faster EPS growth expectations (16.8% vs 14.7%), higher value-added services revenue contribution (41.2% of total), and strategic advantages through its Agent Pay platform and BVNK acquisition. Mastercard is rated as the more attractive opportunity despite both stocks carrying a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges XTI Aerospace, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against XTI Aerospace, Inc. alleging that company executives made materially false statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts about the business during the period of April 15, 2026 to August 17, 2026. The complaint specifically alleges undisclosed executive activities, ineffective disclosure controls, and inability to timely file earnings reports. Investors have until October 27, 2026 to request appointment as lead plaintiff.

items.title: Snowflake vs. Adobe: Which Enterprise AI Stock Is a Better Buy?
items.summary: Snowflake is positioned as the stronger enterprise AI play with accelerating growth (37% product revenue YoY), robust customer expansion (32% net additions YoY), and strong AI adoption metrics. Adobe faces headwinds from slower near-term monetization and moderating RPO growth despite expanding its AI portfolio. Snowflake carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) while Adobe holds Rank #3 (Hold).

items.title: Why Union Pacific (UNP) is a Great Dividend Stock Right Now
items.summary: Union Pacific (UNP), a railroad company in the Transportation sector, is highlighted as a compelling dividend investment with a 2% yield and an annualized dividend of $5.68, up 4.4% year-over-year. The company has increased dividends 3 times over the last 5 years with an average annual increase of 7.19%. With a 45% payout ratio and expected earnings growth of 11.66% for 2026, UNP presents a strong dividend play, though it currently holds a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold).

items.title: AMKR or LSCC: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
items.summary: In a comparison of two Electronics-Semiconductors stocks, Amkor Technology (AMKR) emerges as the superior value option over Lattice Semiconductor (LSCC). AMKR holds a Zacks Rank of #1 (Strong Buy) with improving earnings outlook, while LSCC has a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold). AMKR's valuation metrics are significantly more attractive, featuring a forward P/E of 17.82 versus LSCC's 50.04, a PEG ratio of 0.57 versus 0.85, and a P/B ratio of 2.46 versus 18.53, earning AMKR a Value grade of B compared to LSCC's F grade.

items.title: Keysight's 56% Order Jump Puts AI Demand and Q4 Guidance in Focus
items.summary: Keysight Technologies posted strong Q3 results with orders surging 56% to $2.091B, driven by AI infrastructure and advanced connectivity demand. The company expects Q4 revenues of $1.930B-$1.950B, though supply constraints may limit near-term conversion of the expanded backlog. Software and services grew double digits, representing 33% of revenues with 24% annual recurring revenue.

items.title: Keysight Falls 11.1% in 3 Months While AI Demand Keeps Accelerating
items.summary: Keysight Technologies (KEYS) shares declined 11.1% over three months despite Q3 revenues rising 36% and non-GAAP EPS jumping 79%. Orders surged 56% to a record $2.091B driven by AI infrastructure and connectivity demand. However, supply constraints, policy uncertainty, and a declining recurring-revenue mix present headwinds. The stock trades at 22.6X forward earnings, below historical averages but above sector comparisons, presenting a balanced rather than bargain valuation.

items.title: CEO of Iconic Railroad Stock Unloads More Than 1,000 Shares
items.summary: Norfolk Southern CEO Mark R. George sold 1,035 shares worth ~$335,000 on September 13, 2026, to cover tax liabilities from vesting restricted stock units. Despite the sale, his direct holdings increased to 22,783 shares. The article notes NSC has underperformed the S&P 500 since 2021, with declining operating margins and net income, though revenue has grown modestly.

items.title: Credo Powers AI Networks With New 1.6T ZeroFlap Optics Launch
items.summary: Credo Technology Group launched its new 224G ZeroFlap optical transceivers supporting 1.6T port speeds for AI architectures. The products integrate DSPs with silicon photonics PICs to reduce insertion loss and improve link margin. Credo expects optical revenue above $600 million in fiscal 2027 with over 85% full-year revenue growth, though it faces intense competition from Marvell Technology and Astera Labs in the high-speed optical networking market.

items.title: Kaplan Fox Encourages Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE: BE) Investors Seeking Recovery to Contact the Firm Before September 28, 2026
items.summary: Kaplan Fox has filed a class action lawsuit against Bloom Energy Corporation on behalf of investors who purchased securities between February 27, 2025 and July 8, 2026. The complaint alleges that the company made false and misleading statements regarding its reliance on Chinese scandium, obtained through intermediaries, and understated its dependence on Chinese sources. The lead plaintiff deadline is September 28, 2026.

items.title: CME vs. Morningstar: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: CME Group and Morningstar are compared as financial infrastructure plays. CME dominates derivatives trading with an impressive 62% net margin and $6.5B revenue, but trades at a premium valuation (forward P/E 22.5). Morningstar offers investment research with lower margins (15.3%) but more attractive valuation (forward P/E 15.5). The author leans toward CME despite valuation concerns due to its superior profitability and dividend, though both stocks have underperformed the S&P 500 over longer periods.

items.title: Tim Cook's Most Defining Move at Apple Has Nothing to Do With AI
items.summary: Tim Cook's most significant achievement at Apple was launching the wearables segment with the Apple Watch in 2014-2015, not AI innovation. This strategic move expanded Apple's ecosystem with health and wellness features, integrated with iOS, and inspired the formalized Apple Services segment. The wearables strategy, combined with services like Apple Pay and Apple Music, drove Apple's stock up over 2,200% during Cook's tenure and established a sustainable competitive advantage that should continue benefiting the company under new CEO John Ternus.

items.title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: Uber, GameStop and Celsius
items.summary: Three CEOs made significant share purchases, signaling confidence in their companies' long-term prospects. Uber CEO bought 141k shares following strong quarterly results with 24% YoY gross bookings growth and record free cash flow. GameStop CEO purchased 1 million shares, while Celsius CEO bought 18k shares. Insider buying is viewed as a positive indicator for longer-term outlook.

items.title: Prediction: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Will Dispose of One of Berkshire Hathaway's Largest Holdings
items.summary: Greg Abel, who took over as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway on December 31, is expected to continue selling the company's Bank of America stake. Berkshire has already sold 549.5 million BofA shares (53% of its position) since June 2024, driven by the bank's valuation reaching a 59% premium to book value and reduced interest rate sensitivity following the Fed's rate cuts.

items.title: Zacks Industry Outlook Grupo Cibest, POSCO, Griffon and GPGI
items.summary: The Zacks Diversified Operations industry is experiencing solid momentum driven by manufacturing sector strength, robust aerospace and defense markets, and commercial aviation growth. However, supply-chain disruptions remain a concern. The industry ranks #59 among 247 Zacks industries but has underperformed the S&P 500 by 28.2% over the past year. Four stocks are highlighted as leaders: Grupo Cibest, POSCO Holdings, Griffon Corp, and GPGI Inc.

items.title: Satya Nadella's Microsoft Disclosed Azure Topped $100 Billion in Annual Sales for the First Time -- but MSFT Has Trailed the Market All Year. Is the Stock Still a Buy?

items.summary: The global AI Productivity Tools Market is valued at $11.72 billion in 2025 and expected to reach $69.22 billion by 2035, growing at a 19.50% CAGR. North America leads with 36% market share, while Asia Pacific shows the fastest growth at 21.21% CAGR. Cloud-based deployment dominates at 65% share, with subscription models accounting for 55% of revenue. Key growth drivers include enterprise automation, data analytics, code generation tools, and RPA adoption across industries.

items.title: Hims & Hers Health, Inc. Securities Fraud Class Action Result of Deceptive Privacy and Billing Practices and Over 14% Stock Decline - Investors may Contact Lewis Kahn, Esq., at Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC
items.summary: Hims & Hers Health faces a securities fraud class action lawsuit after the FTC alleged the telehealth provider shared consumers' sensitive health information with third-party advertising platforms while claiming privacy protection, and deceived users about billing and cancellation practices. The stock declined 14.73% on July 29, 2026, following the FTC announcement. Investors who purchased securities between August 4, 2025 and July 29, 2026 can file lead plaintiff applications by November 2, 2026.

items.title: Down 40%, Is Grab Stock a Buy in September?
items.summary: Grab stock has declined 40% and faces headwinds from macroeconomic challenges, including higher oil prices impacting its business. The article examines whether the stock presents a buying opportunity despite recent insider selling activity and the company's struggles.

items.title: Better Buy: Palantir Stock vs. Microsoft Stock
items.summary: The article compares Palantir and Microsoft as investment options, noting that despite being much smaller by revenue, Palantir generates profit margins comparable to Microsoft. The comparison is framed within the context of rising AI effectiveness driving enterprise implementation demand.

items.title: Brookfield Agrees to Acquire Reliance Worldwide Corporation
items.summary: Brookfield announced an agreement to acquire 100% of Reliance Worldwide Corporation, a global plumbing and heating solutions manufacturer, for US$3.38 per share (US$2.8 billion enterprise value). The all-cash transaction is expected to close in Q1 2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. Brookfield plans to leverage its operating expertise to support Reliance's growth in the underpenetrated push-to-connect fittings market.

items.title: Intuitive Machines vs. Vertiv: Which Industrials Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares two industrial stocks: Intuitive Machines (LUNR), which provides lunar infrastructure and NASA contracts, versus Vertiv (VRT), which supplies cooling and power systems for AI data centers. While Intuitive Machines shows strong growth potential with a $1.1B order backlog and expected 2026 revenue to quadruple, it faces high risk from government concentration and speculative lunar markets. Vertiv demonstrates more predictable growth with 28% revenue increase, $1.9B free cash flow, and lower valuation multiples. The article recommends Vertiv as the better buy due to its lower forward P/E ratio, more stable market demand, and stronger financial fundamentals.

items.title: Ouster, Inc. (OUST) Suffers a Larger Drop Than the General Market: Key Insights
items.summary: Ouster, Inc. (OUST) declined 2% to $32.79, underperforming the S&P 500's 0.45% loss. The stock has plummeted 30.48% over the past month, significantly lagging its sector. While revenue is projected to grow 42.17% year-over-year to $56.2 million, the company maintains a negative EPS outlook of -$0.3. Ouster currently holds a Zacks Rank of #4 (Sell).

items.title: Alibaba vs. Uber Technologies: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Alibaba and Uber Technologies as investment options for 2026. Alibaba operates a massive e-commerce and cloud computing ecosystem in China with conservative financials but faces regulatory risks and slowing growth. Uber has a global platform with strong revenue growth (18% YoY) and higher margins (19%), though it faces legal challenges and driver classification issues. The author recommends Uber as the better buy due to its global reach, settled market position, and more attractive valuation metrics despite Alibaba's strong AI cloud segment growing 45% YoY.

items.title: Credo (CRDO) vs. Marvell (MRVL): Which AI Chip Stock Is the Better Buy?
items.summary: Credo Technology and Marvell Technology are compared as AI chip investment options. Credo offers faster near-term growth (87% revenue growth projected for FY2027) with better valuation at 30X forward earnings, but faces concentration risk with 4 customers representing 84% of revenue. Marvell provides broader AI infrastructure exposure with stronger long-term earnings growth but trades at a premium 72X multiple. Both stocks receive a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Kirby McInerney LLP Alerts Investors Who Acquired Bloom Energy Corporation BE Securities Between February 27, 2025 and July 8, 2026 of Pending Lawsuit
items.summary: Law firm Kirby McInerney LLP announced pending securities class action lawsuits against Bloom Energy Corporation for allegedly making false statements about its reliance on Chinese scandium supplies. A short-seller report on July 8, 2026 revealed that Bloom Energy sourced scandium from China through intermediaries despite claiming minimal China supply chain dependence, causing the stock to fall 5.7%. The firm is seeking lead plaintiffs with a September 28, 2026 deadline.

items.title: INVESTOR ALERT: Pomerantz Law Firm Investigates Claims On Behalf of Investors of lululemon athletica inc. - LULU
items.summary: Pomerantz LLP is investigating potential securities fraud claims against lululemon athletica following the company's September 3, 2026 earnings report, which revealed lower-than-expected revenue, sharply reduced full-year guidance, and negative media commentary. The announcement triggered a 17.38% stock price decline ($21.16 per share) on September 4, 2026.

items.title: INVESTOR ALERT: Pomerantz Law Firm Investigates Claims On Behalf of Investors of D-Wave Quantum Inc. - QBTS
items.summary: Pomerantz LLP is investigating D-Wave Quantum Inc. for potential securities fraud following disappointing Q2 2026 earnings results ($3.08M revenue vs. $4.03-4.08M expected) and the resignation of CFO John Markovich. The stock fell 9.28% on earnings miss and 9.51% on the CFO departure announcement.

items.title: INVESTOR ALERT: Pomerantz Law Firm Reminds Investors with Losses on their Investment in Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises, Inc. of Class Action Lawsuit - BW
items.summary: Pomerantz Law Firm has filed class action lawsuits against Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises, Inc. (BW) on behalf of investors who acquired securities between November 5, 2025, and March 11, 2026. The firm is also investigating claims on behalf of investors in Abeona Therapeutics Inc. (ABEO) and has announced a class action lawsuit against AST SpaceMobile, Inc. (ASTS) and certain officers.

items.title: Microsoft Pays Out More in Dividends Than It Spends Buying Back Stock. Here's What That Does for Investors.
items.summary: Microsoft has shifted its capital allocation strategy, now prioritizing dividends over stock buybacks. In fiscal 2026, the company paid $27.0 billion in dividends versus $16.7 billion in buybacks, a reversal from five years prior. The buyback program primarily offsets dilution from employee stock compensation rather than reducing share count, with minimal impact on earnings per share growth, which has been driven almost entirely by business profitability rather than share reduction.

items.title: Boeing vs. Redwire: Which Aerospace Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Boeing and Redwire represent different aerospace investment profiles: Boeing is a recovery play with $89.5B in FY2025 revenue but faces high leverage (10x debt-to-equity) and negative free cash flow, while Redwire is a high-growth space tech company with 10% revenue growth, minimal debt, but significant losses and negative free cash flow. Boeing's strong backlog and market position offer long-term potential despite near-term challenges, while Redwire's recent $1.8B government contract win signals growth prospects in space infrastructure.

items.title: HIMS Investor Alert: Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP Encourages HIMS Investors with Losses to Contact the Firm
items.summary: A securities fraud class action lawsuit has been filed against Hims & Hers Health, Inc. (HIMS) for allegedly making materially false statements about its privacy practices. The FTC accused HIMS of sharing customers' medical information with third-party advertisers including Meta and Snap. Following the FTC lawsuit announcement on July 29, 2026, HIMS stock declined 14.73%. Investors who purchased HIMS securities between August 4, 2025 and July 29, 2026 can seek lead plaintiff status by November 2, 2026.

items.title: BLOOM ENERGY DEADLINE: ROSEN, LEADING INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Bloom Energy Corporation Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - BE
items.summary: A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against Bloom Energy Corporation for allegedly making materially false and misleading statements regarding its supply chain. The company allegedly understated its reliance on scandium sourced from China through intermediaries and made misleading positive statements about its business operations. Investors who purchased securities between February 27, 2025 and July 8, 2026 may be eligible for compensation. The lead plaintiff deadline is September 28, 2026.

items.title: AST SPACEMOBILE, INC. (ASTS) INVESTOR ALERT Investors With Large Losses in AST SpaceMobile, Inc. Should Contact Bernstein Liebhard LLP To Discuss Their Rights
items.summary: A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against AST SpaceMobile, Inc. on behalf of investors who purchased securities between March 4, 2025 and July 15, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that defendants made materially false and misleading statements regarding the company's business operations, growth prospects, and financial stability, causing AST securities to trade at artificially inflated prices. Investors who suffered losses are encouraged to contact Bernstein Liebhard LLP, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 13, 2026.

items.title: PagerDuty's 2026 Outlook: Operational Discipline and New AI Opportunities Sustains Profitable Growth Model
items.summary: PagerDuty has achieved five consecutive quarters of GAAP profitability and generated $33 million in free cash flow, earning a Superscore of 72. However, revenue growth has stalled at less than 1% year-over-year, and the company faces competitive pressure from platform giants bundling incident response tools. The company is transitioning to consumption-based pricing and positioning AI as a growth driver to reignite expansion.

items.title: KeyCorp Raises 2026 Revenue Outlook: What's Driving It?
items.summary: KeyCorp raised its 2026 revenue guidance to 8% growth from 7-8%, driven by strong loan growth (4-5%), NII expansion (9-11%), and improved fee income guidance (6-7% adjusted). The Clearwater acquisition and robust investment banking activity support the outlook. NIM is expected to reach 3.00-3.05% by year-end. Peer banks PNC and Citizens Financial also project solid 2026 growth.

items.title: Can 3M Continue Its Strong Capital Returns to Shareholders?
items.summary: 3M Company returned $3.8 billion to shareholders through dividends and buybacks in the first half of 2026, with $1.8 billion remaining under its repurchase authorization. The company expects adjusted operating cash flow of $5.8-$6.0 billion and free cash flow conversion above 100% for 2026, while raising its quarterly dividend by 6.8% in February 2026. Despite trading above industry valuation averages, 3M shares gained 3.6% over the past year compared to a 27.8% industry decline.

items.title: Coherent Stock Declines 24% in a Month: Is This a Buying Opportunity?
items.summary: Coherent Corp (COHR) has experienced a 24% monthly decline after a 155% annual surge. Despite premium valuation, the company's AI-focused portfolio, strong datacenter revenue growth (58.6% YoY), expanding margins, and capacity expansion plans support a positive long-term outlook. The stock is rated a Buy, though risks include hyperscaler spending cycles and customer concentration.

items.title: TJX International's Adjusted Margin Hits 7.3%: More Upside Ahead?
items.summary: TJX Companies' International division achieved significant profitability gains in Q2 FY2027, with adjusted segment profit margin rising 210 basis points year-over-year to 7.3%. The division reported net sales of $2.09 billion, up 11% from the prior year, driven by higher customer transactions and 7% comparable sales growth. The margin improvement was supported by favorable merchandise margins and expense leverage, while the company continued expansion efforts in Europe.

items.title: Realty Income Teams Up With KKR: Can Private Capital Drive Growth?
items.summary: Realty Income will retain 51% ownership of a 54-property European net lease venture while KKR invests €528 million for 49%, with KKR's returns capped at 6.3%-6.5% IRR. The deal reflects Realty Income's shift toward private capital funding, with public equity comprising only 18% of first-half 2026 investments versus a historical 47% average. The company raised its 2026 investment guidance to $10 billion, and the venture is expected to close September 30.

items.title: Digital Realty Expands Into Turkiye With Strategic Data Center JV
items.summary: Digital Realty has announced a strategic joint venture with Ronesans Infrastructure to enter the Turkish market. The partnership will develop a next-generation data center campus in Ankara with over 22MW of carrier-neutral IT capacity, with completion targeted for 2028. Plans also include expansion into Istanbul to create a connected regional infrastructure platform serving cloud, AI, and enterprise digital infrastructure demands.

items.title: CIEN's New Venture Fund: Can it Turn AI Networking Into Growth Engine?
items.summary: Ciena Corporation launched Ciena Ventures, a $200 million corporate venture capital program focused on next-generation connectivity technologies including networking infrastructure, data centers, and optical interconnects. The company expects its addressable market to reach $50 billion by 2029 driven by AI-driven bandwidth demand, with fiscal 2027 revenue projected to grow at least 30% to $8.3-$8.4 billion. However, Ciena faces intense competition from Cisco and Arista Networks in the AI networking space.

items.title: Is This the Right Time to Retain Resmed Stock in Your Portfolio?
items.summary: Resmed is divesting its MatrixCare business for $490 million to streamline its Residential Care Software segment and focus on higher-growth platforms. The company's Masks segment showed strong 13% revenue growth in fiscal 2026, driven by product innovation and improved compliance rates. However, macroeconomic pressures and intense competition pose operational risks.

items.title: Netlist vs. Sandisk: Which AI Memory Stock Is the Better Buy?
items.summary: Netlist and Sandisk are both capitalizing on AI-driven demand for advanced memory technologies. Netlist has tripled revenues to $214.7M in H1 2026 with a strategic Samsung alliance, but relies heavily on DRAM resales. Sandisk shows stronger scale with datacenter revenues up 103% sequentially and $93.9B in forward revenue commitments through new business models. Netlist trades at a lower valuation (2.33X forward sales vs. 4.44X for Sandisk) and carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) versus Sandisk's Rank #3 (Hold).

items.title: Credo vs. Broadcom: Which AI Connectivity Stock Is the Better Pick?
items.summary: Credo Technology and Broadcom are both benefiting from the AI infrastructure buildout, but with different strategies. Credo shows stronger growth momentum with 115% revenue growth and 48.2% operating margins, while Broadcom offers massive scale with $16.7B in AI chip revenues and 67.9% operating margins. Both stocks carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, with Credo trading at a slightly lower valuation multiple (9.5X vs 9.93X forward sales).

items.title: Atlassian vs. ServiceNow: Which Cloud Software Stock Has an Edge?
items.summary: Atlassian and ServiceNow are both benefiting from AI adoption in enterprise software, but they face different near-term dynamics. Atlassian shows stronger execution with 31% cloud revenue growth driven by its Rovo AI product and larger customer deals, while trading at a more attractive 5.96X forward sales multiple. ServiceNow's AI ACV exceeded $1 billion with strong adoption, but faces margin pressure from rising AI consumption and hyperscaler reliance. Atlassian receives a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) versus ServiceNow's #4 (Sell), giving TEAM a clearer edge.

items.title: In National Advertising Division Challenge, Zuru Voluntarily Modifies Challenged Incentivized Review Practices
items.summary: Zuru Edge Limited has voluntarily discontinued its incentivized review program and modified practices to comply with FTC Endorsement Guides following a challenge by Procter & Gamble. The company ran a Facebook group for six years offering product reimbursement to reviewers without requiring disclosure of this material connection. Zuru has now discontinued the group and implemented clear disclosure requirements for future incentivized reviews.

items.title: Chewy vs. TJX Companies: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Chewy, a digital-first pet retailer with an 8.6B market cap, against TJX Companies, a brick-and-mortar off-price retail powerhouse with a 139B market cap. While Chewy offers a cheaper P/S ratio (0.7x vs 2.3x) and growing Autoship subscription revenue, TJX demonstrates superior profitability with a 9.1% net margin versus Chewy's 1.8%, a lower P/E ratio (23.3x vs 32.65x), and stronger free cash flow ($4.9B vs $562.4M). The author recommends TJX Companies as the better buy, citing its consistent ability to beat expectations, strong customer demand for value, and proven track record of profitability across economic cycles.

items.title: BAC Warns of Q3 Capital Markets Weakness: Will Fee Income Take a Hit?
items.summary: Bank of America expects Q3 investment banking fees of $1.6-$1.8B, down ~15% year-over-year, with trading revenues flat. However, wealth management AUM fees projected to rise 10-15% should offset some weakness. CEO Moynihan noted a 'very strong' deal pipeline, suggesting the slowdown may be timing-related rather than structural.

items.title: 2 Non-AI Giants to Buy on Solid Guidance and Lucrative Valuation
items.summary: Centene Corp. and Archer-Daniels-Midland Co. have both raised their 2026 guidance with significant earnings improvements. Despite year-to-date gains exceeding 50%, both stocks maintain attractive valuations and hold Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) ratings, suggesting further upside potential for the remainder of 2026.

items.title: 3 AI Stocks Poised to Outperform Micron and Sandisk as the Next Infrastructure Bottleneck Builds
items.summary: As AI infrastructure demands evolve beyond chips and memory, three companies are positioned to capitalize on emerging bottlenecks: Innodata provides data organization services with 58% revenue growth; Nebius offers neocloud services with expanding data center capacity and rising per-megawatt contract values; and Vertiv supplies critical liquid cooling solutions for AI infrastructure with 24% revenue growth and accelerating demand.

items.title: The AI Company You Haven't Heard of -- But Should Keep on Your Radar
items.summary: Bloom Energy, a fuel-cell technology company founded in 2001, is positioned to benefit significantly from AI infrastructure expansion. The company helps data centers obtain electricity faster by generating power on-site, addressing grid capacity constraints. After years of losses, Bloom Energy achieved profitability in early 2026 with 166% revenue growth in Q2, driven by major enterprise customers like Oracle. As data center power consumption is projected to reach 12% of U.S. electricity by 2030, Bloom Energy could become a standard supplier in the rapidly expanding data-center ecosystem.

items.title: Oligonucleotide Therapeutics Market Outlook 2026-2035 - Featuring Profiles of Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, Ionis Pharmaceuticals, and Sarepta Therapeutics
items.summary: The global oligonucleotide therapeutics market is projected to grow from USD 7.7 billion in 2025 to USD 72.1 billion by 2035, expanding at a 23.4% CAGR. Growth is driven by advances in RNA-based medicine, targeted delivery technologies, expanding applications beyond rare diseases into chronic and metabolic conditions, and increasing regulatory approvals. Antisense oligonucleotides lead the market at 39.9% share, while subcutaneous administration dominates at 56.4%. North America commands 57.9% market share.

items.title: Is a Sandisk Stock Split Coming?
items.summary: Sandisk's stock price has surged to $1,552, prompting speculation about a potential stock split. While no split has been announced, the article explains that a split would be purely cosmetic—it wouldn't change the company's fundamentals, revenue, profits, or shareholder value. The main practical impact would be on options traders and potentially on Sandisk's eligibility for the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which weights stocks by share price rather than market value.
